report:
# When Do Obligations for High-Risk AI Systems in Annex III of the EU AI Act Apply?

## Executive Summary
Under the AI Act as originally adopted in 2024, Annex III high-risk AI obligations were scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026, 36 months after the Regulation's entry into force (medium confidence). Following the "AI Omnibus" amendment, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, this date was extended: Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from 2 December 2027, with obligations for products embedding high-risk AI (Annex I) delayed to 2 August 2028 (high confidence). A cluster of low-confidence, unverifiable sources claims a further extension to 2 August 2029, but this is not corroborated by any official EU source.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Pre-Omnibus)
The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with prohibitions on unacceptable-risk AI applying from 2 February 2025 and GPAI/governance obligations applying from 2 August 2025 (low confidence) ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)). As originally drafted, obligations for high-risk systems were to become applicable 36 months after entry into force (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)). The bulk of Annex III rules were in turn scheduled to take effect on 2 August 2026 (medium confidence), a date repeated across numerous pre-Omnibus legal and industry sources ([AI Act Explorer](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The Digital Omnibus on AI was adopted on 19 November 2025, reached political agreement between Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The Commission proposed—and the co-legislators agreed—to extend the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months, tying entry into application to Commission confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools are ready (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Current Applicable Dates
As amended, Annex III high-risk AI obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), per multiple official EU guidance pages ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [Timeline Tool](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). Obligations for high-risk AI embedded in regulated products under Annex I apply later, from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27.07.2026) confirms that systems already on the market are only subject to Chapter III rules if they undergo significant design changes after the Article 113 application date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Some commentary frames 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 as "backstop dates" that would have applied automatically had the Omnibus not been approved before August 2026 (low confidence) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

### Scope Clarification
Annex III lists categories of AI use cases (e.g., hiring, education, credit scoring, essential services) that *can* be classified as high-risk, rather than systems automatically deemed high-risk (low confidence) ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- **2026 vs. 2027 discrepancy**: Several undated or pre-Omnibus sources still cite 2 August 2026 as the Annex III deadline, while official post-Omnibus EU guidance confirms 2 December 2027. This appears to reflect outdated content rather than a genuine conflict ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20) vs. [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).
- **Disputed 2029 date (low confidence, 0.21 and below)**: Three news/blog sources claim a second amendment pushed the deadline to 2 August 2029, citing unready standards and notified bodies. No official EU source corroborates this, and two of the three cited sources use placeholder/example domains, raising serious doubts about their reliability.
- **Unupdated official page**: The AI Act Service Desk's Article 111 page still cites 2 August 2026 (medium confidence, 0.68), inconsistent with other official pages reflecting the Omnibus update, suggesting incomplete synchronization across EU guidance resources.
- **Low-confidence framing claims**: The "backstop dates" characterization (0.12) and the Annex III scope clarification (0.18) are both flagged as low confidence and should be treated as plausible interpretation rather than established fact.

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether the 2 August 2029 date is a real, adopted legal change or an error/rumor; no official source confirms it.
- The precise legislative instrument and procedural status underpinning the 2 December 2027 date is not fully documented in available excerpts.
- Whether all EU guidance pages have been uniformly updated post-Omnibus.
- What specific readiness conditions (standards, notified bodies) the Commission must confirm before enforcement begins, and whether these have been met.
- How ongoing monitoring of standards/notified-body readiness could trigger further delays.

# When Do Obligations for High-Risk AI Systems in Annex III of the EU AI Act Apply?

## Executive Summary
Under the AI Act as originally adopted in 2024, Annex III high-risk AI obligations were scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026, 36 months after the Regulation's entry into force (high/medium confidence). Following the "AI Omnibus" amendment, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, this date was extended: Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from 2 December 2027, with obligations for products embedding high-risk AI (Annex I) delayed to 2 August 2028 (high confidence). A cluster of low-confidence, unverifiable sources claims a further extension to 2 August 2029, but this is not corroborated by any official EU source.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Pre-Omnibus)
The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with staggered application dates: prohibitions on unacceptable-risk AI from 2 February 2025 and governance/GPAI obligations from 2 August 2025 (low confidence) ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)). As originally drafted, obligations for high-risk systems were to become applicable 36 months after entry into force (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)), with the bulk of Annex III rules set to take effect on 2 August 2026 (medium confidence), a date repeated across numerous pre-Omnibus legal and industry sources ([AI Act Explorer](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The Digital Omnibus on AI was adopted on 19 November 2025, reached political agreement between Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The Commission proposed—and the co-legislators agreed—to extend the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months, tying entry into application to Commission confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools are ready (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Current Applicable Dates
As amended, Annex III high-risk AI obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), per multiple official EU guidance pages ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [Timeline Tool](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). Obligations for high-risk AI embedded in regulated products under Annex I apply later, from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27.07.2026) confirms that systems already on the market are only subject to Chapter III rules if they undergo significant design changes after the Article 113 application date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Some commentary frames 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 as "backstop dates" that would have applied automatically had the Omnibus not been approved before August 2026 (low confidence) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

### Scope Clarification
Annex III lists categories of AI use cases (e.g., hiring, education, credit scoring, essential services) that *can* be classified as high-risk, rather than systems automatically deemed high-risk (low confidence) ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- **2026 vs. 2027 discrepancy**: Several undated or pre-Omnibus sources still cite 2 August 2026 as the Annex III deadline, while official post-Omnibus EU guidance confirms 2 December 2027. This appears to reflect outdated content rather than a genuine conflict ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20) vs. [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).
- **Disputed 2029 date**: Three news/blog sources (low confidence, 0.12–0.21) claim a second amendment pushed the deadline to 2 August 2029, citing unready standards and notified bodies. No official EU source corroborates this, and two of the three cited sources use placeholder/example domains, raising serious doubts about their reliability.
- **Unupdated official page**: The AI Act Service Desk's Article 111 page still cites 2 August 2026, inconsistent with other official pages reflecting the Omnibus update, suggesting incomplete synchronization across EU guidance resources.

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether the 2 August 2029 date is a real, adopted legal change or an error/rumor; no official source confirms it.
- The precise legislative instrument and procedural status underpinning the 2 December 2027 date is not fully documented in available excerpts.
- Whether all EU guidance pages have been uniformly updated post-Omnibus.
- What specific readiness conditions (standards, notified bodies) the Commission must confirm before enforcement begins, and whether these have been met.
- How ongoing monitoring of standards/notified-body readiness could trigger further delays.
